summary: Motion subjects and paths occur with zero marking, b-, ʕal-, me-bayn and bayn; route resumption is visible in 77/97 and probably 79/18. Overtaking is already represented in the entry and has both suffixed and overt noun complements.
Temporal I describes an interval elapsing; temporal III treats life or a season as object with L-series agents in Preterit. The winter/life examples are not evidence of an additional stem.
Infectum with ko-/g- occurs in past narrative as well as prospective contexts. Infectum-wa explicitly supplies recurring passage; no blanket tense inference is drawn from the edition translation.

Read-only lookup confirms špʕ is absent from the supplied glossary while šfʕ itself includes p-spellings. Retain inherited cross-reference and head; do not fabricate a duplicate entry or conflate spelling with a new root.
Existing blank sense I.3 is preserved. New numbered senses begin at I.4; all inherited numbers remain stable.

Twelve compact records omit verse text. For those, only supplied classifications can be retained provisionally; Talay 1/294 can additionally be checked against its full companion record and requires Infectum.
Does the inherited blank I.3 have an intended gloss in the editors' source?
Should the dangling cross-reference to špʕ be removed or resolved by an editorial alias? No separate entry was retrievable.
Is šofəʕ b-qamuṯ- conventional for interrupting speech, and is šapiʕinanne in 79/18 a finite motion form with route resumption -nne?
At 106/28 does final -i represent an indefinite plural agent, local morphology, or a transcription issue? It contrasts with the German singular husband.
At Hors 1/5 is hawi in the inherited EL 5 quotation editorial supplementation? The supplied verse has no hawi; no silent text replacement is proposed.
At 78/104 what is the exact object ending and collective/plural reference? The supplied mašpeʕəlle differs from inherited mašpéʕi-le.
Does 113/155 describe archery, a sexual metaphor, or both? xəzenayḏa is glossed parenthetically as vulva only in German.
Restore the missing d in Geldbrieftasche
rationale: The word is Geldbrieftasche, as also printed in the matching edition translation at 55/8; the entry has dropped d.

summary: Correct the malformed German clause about the car
rationale: The independent clause needs the finite verb fuhr after its subject; zor is a typo for vor. The supplied Turoyo mhalaxla b-qamuṯan describes the car travelling in front of us. No change is proposed to the following parenthetical clause.

summary: Literal passage includes vehicles, animals, projectiles, a river and drops of water, and depicted travellers; these participant changes do not establish additional senses.
Running a vehicle over a person with ʕal- is retained as compositional passage along a path, already exemplified by EL 16; no duplicated sense or quotation.
A projectile can be the understood moving participant in caused passage; 113/155 alone does not establish a technical archery sense or the sexual reading independently of the German parenthesis.
